issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a 'Stock' class (with methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock), but the template and solution repositories provide an 'Inventory' class that implements those methods while the Stock.java file in the template/solution is empty. This name/type mismatch between 'Stock' (spec) and 'Inventory' (code) is likely to confuse students about which class to modify/use and where the stock functionality actually resides.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock', or (B) rename Inventory.java to Stock.java (and update its class name/usages) and remove or implement the empty Stock.java. Ensure the UML, template files, and example solution consistently use the same class name so students clearly know which class to modify and use.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (and ask students to modify/use Stock and a static Stock stock in SealSaloon), but the provided template and solution implement the same functionality in a class named Inventory. This mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) creates confusion: students may look for a Stock implementation, find an empty Stock.java file, and not realize Inventory is the intended class representing the saloon's stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Either (A) rename the Inventory class (and file) in the template and solution to Stock so it matches the problem statement/UML, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to consistently refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Ensure SealSaloon and examples use the same class name for the shared stock to avoid student confusion.
